Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state any country or model scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar things with an unexpected design or function.
Hook: generate five declarative candidates; select a concrete subject-first hook, preferably 6–10 words, maximum 12 only with the existing justified exception. No questions or generic trivia setup. Show the surprise without explaining the mechanism early.

Target 25–29 seconds including the configured channel sign-off, hard maximum 30. Preserve spoken/display copy, voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. Do not add a separate generic CTA.

Packaging claim: Road Signs Can Shine Without Their Own Power
Core fact: Retroreflective sign materials direct vehicle headlight light back toward the source, making signs look bright to the driver.
Second reveal: The material can use tiny beads or microprismatic elements; the sign is not generating its own light.
First-frame and mechanism proof: A real unpowered retroreflective road sign already shining in headlights; then compare it with the same sign outside the beam. Macro material proof must match beads or prisms actually described.
Search queries: retroreflective road sign night; headlights road sign reflection; traffic sign close up reflective
Fact boundaries: Do not imply every glowing roadside object is unpowered or that the material reflects all light equally in every direction.
